question: Does there exist a computable cognitive architecture with a strict capability advantage over defined DNN or Transformer baselines under explicit resource bounds, with a credible path to approximately 20 W continuous operation?

baselines.version_policy: Pin model, implementation, weights, tokenizer, and revision per experiment.
Select a task-appropriate strong non-Transformer neural baseline and pin its full configuration.

criteria.description: The candidate has executable operational semantics or a reduction to a known computable model.
criteria.indicator: Executable reference implementation or checkable reduction artifact
criteria.threshold: At least one independent replay completes on a finite input
criteria.falsifier: No finite operational semantics or computable reduction can be specified

criteria.description: The candidate transfers across heterogeneous pre-registered task families.
criteria.indicator: Held-out performance across at least three heterogeneous task families
criteria.threshold: Meets every pre-registered family threshold without candidate-specific retraining
criteria.falsifier: Competence remains confined to one task family or relies on test contamination

criteria.description: The candidate establishes a strict separation against named reproducible baselines.
criteria.indicator: Checked bound, verified algorithmic result, or pre-registered Pareto analysis
criteria.threshold: Strictly improves at least one declared resource without violating capability constraints
criteria.falsifier: The advantage disappears under matched resources, stronger baselines, or replication

criteria.description: The candidate has bounded energy accounting and an explicit scaling path.
criteria.indicator: Idle, active, average power and joules per task at a declared system boundary
criteria.threshold: Measured or uncertainty-bounded model supports a route to 20 W continuous operation
criteria.falsifier: Whole-system scaling cannot approach 20 W without losing required capability

criteria.description: The candidate declares observations that cause rejection or downgrade.
criteria.threshold: Every promoted claim has at least one executable or formally checkable falsifier
criteria.falsifier: A claim remains compatible with every possible observation

glossary.definition: Whether a behaviour can be produced by a finite effective procedure.
Resources required by an algorithm as its input or task scale changes.
Resources and evidence required to acquire a target behaviour.
Breadth of competence and transfer across heterogeneous task families.
Ability to continue selecting actions and learning with bounded external intervention.
Useful capability delivered per declared unit of resource.
Whether a computation can plausibly be embodied within declared physical constraints.
